minutes.headline: Sewer Commission backed an 8% FY23 rate increase and kept grease trap fees only for non-compliant customers.
minutes.summary: The commission discussed and voted by roll call on an 8% sewer rate increase for FY23, which reduces the projected retained-earnings loss. It then set grease trap permit fees to apply only to non-compliant customers, and reviewed proposed policy and bylaw changes to send to counsel and the bylaw review committee. Warrant articles, ARPA project ideas and the DPW director's resignation were also covered.

votes.motion: Accept an 8% sewer rate increase for FY23.
Drop the annual grease trap permit fees for customers in compliance for FY23.
Charge non-compliant customers a grease trap fee for FY23 under Lunenburg grease trap regulations, for internal and external traps.
Accept all policy changes except the grease trap policy and the pipe size and slope spec changes.
Approve all four bylaw categories as discussed, so the business manager can go to counsel.
Approve the already-approved changes (Chapter 147, reconnection fee, grease trap annual fee) and send them forward.

budget_items.what_was_said: The draft budget kept the capital plan and engineering lines as is; unspent amounts would return to retained earnings. Summary columns for an 8% and a 6% increase were added.
With the 8% increase the projected loss for next year drops from the earlier figure.
The 8% increase would raise the rate and the typical quarterly bill by roughly ten to fifteen dollars.
The budget assumes annual fees charged at the non-compliant rate. Members discussed raising them but agreed to hold the current regulation amounts until the policy review.
The minimum quarterly charge applies when a customer connects mid-quarter. Members favored monthly proration over daily.
Well-water sewer billing is based on a fixed usage figure unchanged since the commission began, and members chose to keep it with hardship appeals.
A reconnection fee change for sewer work needing inspections was already approved on 2/8/22.
The usual percentage transfer to capital reserve will again be a warrant article alongside the budget and OPEB.
Monthly and quarterly invoices were reviewed from the commission's own flow data and noted as okayed.

decisions.decision: Final FY23 budget vote set for the March 8 meeting; the business manager will send a revised budget with the 8% increase beforehand.
Well pricing policy stays as is, with the commission willing to hear hardship cases.
Grease trap policy stays as is for now; a joint session with the Board of Health will be sought on fines and inspections.
Meeting with the Finance Committee set for March 24.
Proration of bills to be monthly, not daily.

what_happened.line: The commission voted by roll call on an 8% sewer rate increase for FY23; the minutes do not state the result.
It voted to drop annual grease trap permit fees for customers in compliance and to charge a fee only to non-compliant customers; results were not stated.
Members voted item by item on policy changes for counsel and the bylaw review committee, leaving the grease trap policy and pipe size and slope specs out.
Bills will be prorated monthly rather than daily, and well-water sewer billing stays on its current basis, with hardship cases to be heard.
The final FY23 budget vote is set for the March 8 meeting, with a revised budget showing the 8% increase to be sent beforehand.

why_it_matters: An 8% rate increase would raise the typical quarterly sewer bill by roughly ten to fifteen dollars, and the vote that sets it is still ahead.
Grease trap fees would fall on customers found non-compliant rather than on every customer, and bill proration and well-water billing rules shape what some households owe.
